data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 proposes distinguishing genuine from coincidental panel reliability by whether panel errors are structured (genuine causal model) vs random (mere correlational filter). But this diagnostic is unsound for the problem's requirement: a correlational checklist that systematically tracks the right answer can produce structured errors that mirror the task's structure, because surface regularities often correlate with causal dependencies. Conversely, a genuine causal-model checklist can produce random-looking errors if it handles most causal links correctly and fails on rare independent cases. Thus error structure within a single evaluation cannot reliably map to causal vs correlational status as the target claims, so it fails to provide a valid single-evaluation distinguishing criterion.
